item.title: Day 3 · Bonnie Greer, British-American author and critic, dies aged 77 (BBC)
item.description:
The pioneering novelist and theatre critic, first black president of the Edinburgh International Festival, has died.

British-American author and critic Bonnie Greer dies aged 77

16 September 2026

Paul Glynn, Culture reporter

Getty Images: Greer’s work often tackled topics around culture, race and public institutions

British-American author and cultural commentator Bonnie Greer has died at the age of 77 after a brief illness, her husband has said.

In a statement delivered with “profound sadness”, Greer’s widower David Hutchins noted how the acclaimed playwright and critic had made “an enduring contribution to British cultural and public life” with her “intelligence, courage and distinctive voice”.

He added: “To me, she was my partner, confidante and inspiration, and I feel profoundly privileged to have shared my life with her.”

Hutchins continued: “Those closest to Bonnie will remember her warmth, humour, generosity and extraordinary ability to bring people together.”

‘Courage, humour and humanity’

BBC presenter Clive Myrie led the tributes from elsewhere, posting on X: “This is such a shock. She was a friend and mentor and I will miss her with all my heart.”

Former deputy prime minister David Lammy called Greer “a powerful wordsmith and artist, she was eloquent and exacting”.

He added that she was “a true life force” and he would “never forget her quiet fearlessness taking on Nick Griffin” during an appearance with the then-British National Party (BNP) leader on the BBC’s Question Time in 2009.

Lammy added: “I will miss her mentorship, and her friendship.”

London Mayor Sadiq Khan said Greer’s voice brought “courage, humour and humanity to Britain’s cultural conversation”.

He said: “She inspired and opened doors for so many others. And she was great fun too - I will miss her friendship enormously.”

Plays, novels and panel shows

Born in Chicago in 1948, Greer wrote plays from a young age and went on to study theatre in her home city and before attending the Actors Studio in New York with director Elia Kazan.

Greer moved to the UK in 1986 and became a familiar face on UK TV, appearing as a frequent panellist on programmes like Question Time and Newsnight Review, debating the topics of the day.

She penned award-winning works like Munda Negra, which won her the Verity Bargate Award for best play, and novels such as Hanging by Her Teeth (1994) and Entropy (2009).

Once named by the Observer as one of the country’s leading public intellectuals, Greer’s work - across a range of disciplines and platforms - often tackled issues around culture, race and public institutions.

Getty Images: Greer was made an OBE for services to the arts in 2010

Speaking to the Guardian in 2016 in the aftermath of the Black Lives Matter movement, Greer said: “When I wake up in the morning, I’m just myself. It’s only when I leave the door that I become a black woman to the world.”

She added: “I tell black women all the time, ‘Don’t apologise for yourself and keep your hair nappy. Make sure you are heard’.”

Greer served on the boards of cultural institutions including the British Museum, Royal Opera House and London Film School, and was chancellor of London’s Kingston University.

Her other published works include a memoir titled A Parallel Life and a biography of US poet and playwright Langston Hughes.

Also in 2009, her part-memoir, part-music-history book, Obama Music, was published.

Greer was made an OBE in 2010 for services to the arts.

In 2022, she was appointed as a fellow of the Royal Society of Literature.

Broadcaster and author John Simpson added to the tributes on Wednesday, posting: “So sad to hear of the death of the writer and critic Bonnie Greer.

“She was a good friend, and gave me strong support at a time I needed it. Fiercely intelligent, but always avoided personal attacks. A huge loss.”

Fellow journalist and broadcaster Sangita Myska, who interviewed Greer several times, recalled her as having been a “smart, sassy, firebrand who will be missed from our public discourse”.

confidante n. 知己、密友 女性密友；男性拼 confidant
playwright n. 剧作家 play + wright（匠人）
wordsmith n. 文字大师、文字匠 word + smith（铁匠）

item.title: Day 2 · Emily Wilson to retranslate the Odyssey from scratch (Guardian)
item.description:
The Oxford classicist who made Homer plain-English starts again from scratch.

Emily Wilson to retranslate the Odyssey from scratch

Writer who criticised Christopher Nolan film based on her 2017 translation is working on new version of Homer’s poem

1 September 2026

Emma Loffhagen

Photograph: Matt Rourke/AP

Emily Wilson, the first woman to translate Homer’s Odyssey into English, is to retranslate the ancient Greek epic poem from scratch less than a decade after the publication of her acclaimed version.

The announcement comes after Wilson attracted controversy this summer with a scathing assessment of Christopher Nolan’s blockbuster film adaptation of the Odyssey, which she slammed for its “abysmal” writing and lack of sex scenes.

Wilson’s 2017 translation became a bestseller and was praised for making the 3,000-year-old epic poem modern and accessible.

“I’m now retranslating the Odyssey from scratch, with an approach closer to that of my translation of the Iliad, using somewhat more lines than the original, enabling more varied word-length and pacing,” she told the New York Times.

“It’s a complete retranslation. It’s not a revision of the old version,” she told the AP. “I’m about halfway through.”

Nolan cited Wilson’s 2017 translation, including its opening sentence, “Tell me about a complicated man”, as an influence on his adaptation of the poem, released in July this year and starring Tom Holland, Zendaya, Matt Damon and Anne Hathaway.

Nolan’s adaptation took the global box office by storm, making $264m (£196m) during its opening weekend, marking the director’s best ever opening. Book sales saw a huge bump too: UK print sales of the poem increased by 1,400% in the four weeks to 25 July compared with the same period in 2025, after the film’s release in the middle of the month.

Wilson made headlines for her attack on Nolan’s version. Writing in the London Review of Books, she said: “Nolan’s Odyssey lacks many of the elements that make the poem great … The writing is abysmal.”

She continued: “None of the characters has convincing motivation for their actions or words. There are no sex scenes, and all the food looks horrible,” adding, “I would be ashamed to have written any part of this script.”

Her criticism attracted strong reactions, including from novelist Joyce Carol Oates, who accused Wilson of “haughty superiority”.

Wilson’s decision to retranslate the poem predates the row over the film. In an interview recorded in the spring for the ancient-history podcast Instant Classics, she discussed her desire to return to Homer and approach the poem differently from her first translation.

“I’m proud of my Odyssey translation … I think there are lots of good things about the kinds of compression and choices that I was forced into,” Wilson said then.

She has indicated that she will “probably” keep the opening line, “Tell me about a complicated man”. Wilson also added that her original translation relied too heavily on the word “slave”, when more precise terminology could have better reflected the different forms of enslavement depicted in the poem.

The new translation will also give readers far more of Wilson’s scholarly commentary. “I’m also going to quadruple the number of endnotes because endnotes are really fun to write,” she said.

While Wilson’s decision to retranslate Homer’s poem is unusual, it is not without precedent.

“Translators quite often rework or rewrite their own previous translations,” said Matthew Reynolds, professor of English and comparative criticism at Oxford University.

“Elizabeth Barrett Browning completely rewrote her translation of Aeschylus’s Prometheus Bound, Ezra Pound repeatedly revised his translations of Guido Cavalcanti, and Yu JongHo (유종호) translated Jane Eyre into Korean first in 1970 and again in 2004.”

He added: “It shows that translation – especially literary translation – is not just a matter of right or wrong, good or bad, but a continual exploratory process of interpretive reimagining and re-making.”

Wilson’s new Odyssey does not yet have a publication date.

生词标注（新闻高频 + 词汇第二义项）

词 词性 中文 备注
retranslate v. 重译、重新翻译 re-（再次）+ translate；名词 retranslation
from scratch 短语 从零开始、从头做起 retranslate from scratch = 推倒重来地重译
scathing adj. 严厉尖刻的 scathing assessment / criticism
slam v. 猛烈抨击 新闻口语，≈ strongly criticise
blockbuster n. 大片；轰动性作品 “票房炸弹”；近义 a box-office hit
box office n. 票房（收入） 第二义项：不是”售票处”
take … by storm 短语 席卷、迅速征服 took the global box office by storm
bump n. （数量的）跃升 a huge bump（本义是”撞、颠簸”）
release n./v. 上映；发行 第二义项：the film’s release = 电影上映
row n. 争吵、风波 读 /raʊ/；英式新闻高频（≠“行列”）
predate v. 早于、先于 pre- + date；反义 postdate
precedent n. 先例 not without precedent = 并非没有先例
rework v. 改写、重做 rework / rewrite a translation
revise v. 修订、修改 第二义项：英式英语里 revise 还指”复习”
haughty adj. 傲慢的、居高临下的 “haughty superiority”傲慢的优越感
abysmal adj. 糟透的 ≈ dreadful、terrible
quadruple v. （使）成四倍 quadruple the number of endnotes
endnote n. 尾注（书末注释） footnote 脚注 vs endnote 尾注

item.title: Day 1 · Ancient Roman shipwreck discovered off Sicily coast (BBC)
item.description:
2000-year-old Roman wreck with amphorae hoard found near Mazara del Vallo.

Ancient Roman shipwreck discovered off Sicily coast

9 August 2026

Ian Aikman and Mimi Swaby, global affairs reporters

Shipwreck with amphorae hoard discovered off Sicily coast

Italian divers have discovered an ancient Roman shipwreck off the coast of Sicily, believed to be more than 2,000 years old.

The vessel was found piled high with hundreds of well-preserved containers, which were used to transport goods such as wine and olive oil.

Italy’s Culture Minister Alessandro Giuli hailed the wreck as “one of the most important underwater archaeological discoveries of recent years”.

Specialist police divers found the ship around 46m (150ft) deep, after a tip-off from fishermen. The wreckage is 21m (69ft) long and 6m (20ft) wide, according to reports in local media.

The culture ministry says it dates from the second or 1st Century BC.

Fisherman and free-diver Giacomo De Mola described stumbling across the historic vessel while surveying the seabed near Mazara del Vallo.

He wrote on social media that he had decided to dive and investigate after seeing something that appeared to be a large rock on his scanner.

“I get closer. And my heart stops. It wasn’t a rock,” he said. Instead, he saw hundreds of amphorae — tall ceramic jars used to store goods in the ancient era, mostly wine, oil or grain.

“This is, without a doubt, the most incredible discovery of my life,” he said. “It’s hard to describe what it feels like to be among the first humans, in nearly 20 centuries, to see that place again.”

Carabinieri via AFP: A diver in full scuba gear on the edge of a small boat in the sea

He posted a video of the wreck, showing eels, snappers and “countless marine life” living among the jars, noting: “The sea never ceases to amaze us. This time we didn’t just find a wreck, we found a piece of our history.”

Specialist divers from the cultural heritage protection arm of Italy’s police, known as the Carabinieri Art Squad, were sent to the site.

Officials say safety measures will be taken to safeguard it while it undergoes investigation, as experts work to determine the nature of the wreck and learn more about its cargo.

The Mediterranean seabed is thought to be scattered with similar ancient wrecks. Another 1st or 2nd Century BC vessel was found north-west of Rome in 2023, again laden with hundreds of amphorae.

In 2018, a Greek merchant ship dating back more than 2,400 years was found lying on its side off the Bulgarian coast. At the time, it was hailed as the world’s oldest-known intact shipwreck.

生词标注（都是雅思/新闻高频）

词 词性 中文 备注
shipwreck n. 沉船；船难 wreck = 残骸
wreckage n. （船/飞机）残骸
vessel n. 船只 正式词 = ship
amphora (复数 amphorae) n. 双耳陶罐 古希腊罗马储酒、油、粮用
hail v. 把……誉为、盛赞 hailed as 被誉为
tip-off n. 线报、举报 口语色彩，新闻爱用
free-diver n. 自由潜水者 不带氧气瓶
seabed n. 海床
survey v. 勘测、勘察 名词是”调查/民意测验”
stumble across 短语 偶然发现 不是摔倒
laden adj. 满载的 load 的形容词形式
scatter v. 散布、散落 be scattered with 遍布
safeguard v. 保护 比 protect 正式
undergo v. 经历、经受 undergo investigation 接受调查
cease v. 停止 never ceases to = 总能……
intact adj. 完好无损的 考古类高频词
cargo n. 货物 船上/飞机上的货
marine life 短语 海洋生物

Specialist divers from the cultural heritage protection arm of Italy’s police, known as the Carabinieri Art Squad, were sent to the site.

Officials say safety measures will be taken to safeguard it while it undergoes investigation, as experts work to determine the nature of the wreck and learn more about its cargo.

The Mediterranean seabed is thought to be scattered with similar ancient wrecks. Another 1st or 2nd Century BC vessel was found north-west of Rome in 2023, again laden with hundreds of amphorae.

In 2018, a Greek merchant ship dating back more than 2,400 years was found lying on its side off the Bulgarian coast. At the time, it was hailed as the world’s oldest-known intact shipwreck.
